summary: SUBSCRIBE_TO_FUNNEL save + activation validation is well-structured: a shared fail-closed resolve helper (resolveSubscribeTarget) is reused by both save (validateSubscribeTarget) and activation (requireSubscribeTargetsActive), mirroring the existing requireFunnel pattern. All three validateSteps callsites updated. No regressions, all funnel tests green.

findings.title: Redundant target re-resolution between validateSteps and requireSubscribeTargetsActive on activate
findings.detail: On activate, validateSteps already resolves each SUBSCRIBE target (existence + project scope), then requireSubscribeTargetsActive resolves the SAME target again to read status. For a funnel with N SUBSCRIBE steps pointing at the same target this is duplicate findById calls. Funnels are capped at 50 steps and activation is a rare author action, so the extra read is negligible. No change required.
findings.reason: Negligible cost (small bounded funnels, rare op); merging the two passes would complicate validateSteps which is shared with update/testRun that must NOT check active-status. Keeping them separate is the correct design per task spec.

findings.title: Self-target at activation resolves to inactive (draft) parent
findings.detail: A funnel with a SUBSCRIBE step pointing at itself, when activated, would hit requireSubscribeTargetsActive while the parent is still draft (status flips after the check) and fail with funnel_subscribe_target_inactive. Task 2 explicitly defers self-target handling to runtime (Decision 8) and instructs NOT to add special self-target logic here.
findings.reason: Per task spec: no special self-target logic in this task; runtime re-enter guard owns it.
